name.text: Finding the mistake in a standard deviation calculation

questiontext.text:
Wanjiku recorded the price of a cup of chai at \({@n@}\) kiosks in Kisumu, and found the standard deviation. Her working has one mistake.

Price of a cup (Ksh, \(x\))1015202530
Number of kiosks (\(f\)){@f[1]@}{@f[2]@}{@f[3]@}{@f[4]@}{@f[5]@}
  1. \(\Sigma f = {@n@}\)
  2. \(\Sigma fx = {@Sfx@}\)
  3. \(\Sigma fx^2 = {@Sfx2s@}\)
  4. \(\bar{x} = {@Sfx@} \div {@n@} [[if test="is(mn=mnr)"]]= {@mnd@}[[else]]\approx {@mnd@}[[/if]]\)
  5. \(\sigma^2 = {@Sfx2s@} \div {@n@} - {@sq5d@} \approx {@v5d@}\)
  6. \(\sigma \approx {@sd6d@}\)

(a) Which step has the mistake?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Give the correct standard deviation in shillings, correct to 2 decimal places.

\(\sigma =\) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Check each step against the method: \(\sigma^2 = \dfrac{\Sigma fx^2}{\Sigma f} - \bar{x}^2\) and \(\sigma = \sqrt{\sigma^2}\). The variance is the mean of the squares minus the square of the mean, and the standard deviation is its square root, in the units of the data.

[[if test="is(er=1)"]]

(a) The mistake is in Step 3. Wanjiku squared each \(fx\). Each term should be \(f \times x^2\), so \(\Sigma fx^2 = {@Sfx2@}\).

[[elif test="is(er=2)"]]

(a) The mistake is in Step 5. Wanjiku subtracted \(\bar{x}\) itself. She should subtract \(\bar{x}^2 \approx {@sqd@}\).

[[else]]

(a) The mistake is in Step 6. The value in Step 5 is the variance; the standard deviation is its square root.

[[/if]]

(b) \[\sigma^2 = \frac{ {@Sfx2@} }{ {@n@} } - \left(\frac{ {@Sfx@} }{ {@n@} }\right)^2 \approx {@vrd@}, \qquad \sigma \approx {@sdd@}\]

questiondescription.text:
Statistics II: finding the mistake in a standard deviation calculation

Grade 12 CBE Core and Essential 3.1: Find the wrong step in a worked standard deviation from a frequency table, and give the correct value.

feedbackvariables.text: ch: if is(ans1="s1") then 1 elseif is(ans1="s2") then 2 elseif is(ans1="s3") then 3 elseif is(ans1="s5") then 5 elseif is(ans1="s6") then 6 else 0;

truefeedback.text: Step 4 is right: \({@Sfx@} \div {@n@}\) is the mean. Look at how \(\Sigma fx^2\) and the variance were found.

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="is(ch=1)"]]

Step 1 is right: the frequencies add to \({@n@}\). Check the later steps against \(\sigma^2 = \Sigma fx^2 \div \Sigma f - \bar{x}^2\).

[[elif test="is(ch=2)"]]

Step 2 is right: \(10 \times {@f[1]@} + 15 \times {@f[2]@} + 20 \times {@f[3]@} + 25 \times {@f[4]@} + 30 \times {@f[5]@} = {@Sfx@}\). Test the later steps in the same way.

[[elif test="is(ch=3)"]]

Step 3 is right: each term is \(f \times x^2\), and \(100 \times {@f[1]@} + 225 \times {@f[2]@} + 400 \times {@f[3]@} + 625 \times {@f[4]@} + 900 \times {@f[5]@} = {@Sfx2@}\). Look at what is done with it afterwards.

[[elif test="is(ch=5) and is(er=1)"]]

Step 5 uses the right method on the numbers from the steps before it: \(\Sigma fx^2 \div \Sigma f - \bar{x}^2\), with \(\bar{x}^2 \approx {@sq5d@}\). If its result is wrong, one of those numbers is wrong.

[[elif test="is(ch=5)"]]

Step 5 is right: it is the mean of the squares minus the square of the mean, \({@Sfx2@} \div {@n@} - {@sq5d@}\). What should be done with this value next?

[[elif test="is(ch=6)"]]

Step 6 takes the square root of the value in Step 5, \(\sqrt{ {@v5d@} } \approx {@sd6d@}\), which is the right thing to do. The mistake is in a value found before that.

[[else]]

Check each step against \(\sigma^2 = \Sigma fx^2 \div \Sigma f - \bar{x}^2\) and \(\sigma = \sqrt{\sigma^2}\).

[[/if]]

truefeedback.text: That is Wanjiku's answer, which contains the mistake. Correct the step you found and recalculate.
You divided by \(n - 1 = {@n-1@}\). In this book the variance divides by \(\Sigma f = {@n@}\).

falsefeedback.text: \(\sigma^2 = \Sigma fx^2 \div \Sigma f - \bar{x}^2\), then take the square root. Give it to 2 decimal places.
